title: Angle sum of a triangle
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:55Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank's only candidate, the sine rule, is a Year 11 and 12 trigonometry idea at a much greater depth than the Year 7 point that the angles of a triangle sum to 180°, so no bank point teaches this idea.

draft.title: Angle sum of a triangle
card: The three angles inside any triangle add to 180°. This is true for every triangle, whatever its shape or size.
To find a missing angle, add the two angles you know. Then subtract that total from 180°.
Example: a triangle has angles of 50° and 65°. Add them: 50° + 65° = 115°. The third angle is 180° − 115° = 65°.
A right angle is 90°. If a triangle has a right angle, the other two angles add to 90°.
draft.remember: Add the two known angles, then take the total away from 180°.

a.q: A triangle has angles of 70° and 45°. What is the third angle?
a.why: 70° + 45° = 115°, and 180° − 115° = 65°. The answer 115° is wrong because it is only the sum of the two known angles, and the step of subtracting from 180° was skipped.
a.clue: Add the two angles you know, then subtract from 180°.

b.q: Mia cuts a triangle of card in Hobart. One angle is a right angle and another is 38°. What is the size of the third angle?
b.why: A right angle is 90°, so 90° + 38° = 128°. Then 180° − 128° = 52°. The answer 142° comes from subtracting 38° from 180° and forgetting the right angle.
b.clue: A right angle is 90°, so use it as one of the known angles.
